I don't have any commentary notes on Hosea 10 for you yet. My only attempt to fetch sources failed, and the tool won't let me make another call in this reply. I read no source pages.

**What happened:** I asked six pages for their content at once: Enduring Word, Precept Austin, Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, and the NET Bible notes. The pages came back in a different format than my code expected, so it crashed before saving or showing any text. When I tried to look at what had come back, the tool refused because I had used up my calls for this reply. As a result I can't tell you what any of those sources say about Hosea 10.

Your rules say to use only what the pages actually say and to give a URL for every point. Writing notes from memory and labelling them as Gill or Enduring Word would break both rules, so I've left the notes out.

**What I'll do when you reply (for example, "continue"):**
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** fetch and read Enduring Word, Precept Austin, and Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on biblehub.com, plus StudyLight if needed.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** search the Reformed, Baptist, Wesleyan, Pentecostal and Lutheran sites. The verses most likely to come up are v. 12 ("Sow for yourselves righteousness… until He comes and sends righteousness upon you like rain"), which touches on grace, effort and repentance, and v. 8 ("Cover us! … Fall on us!"), which Luke 23:30 and Revelation 6:16 quote. I'll only report a difference if the sites actually show one.
3. **Other views:**
   - Modern scholarship: the NET Bible notes on hard wording such as v. 1 ("luxuriant" or "empty" vine), v. 10 ("double transgression") and v. 14 (Shalman and Beth-arbel), plus Bible Odyssey on Bethel, Beth-aven and the calf worship.
   - Catholic and Orthodox: the Church Fathers on newadvent.org, and catholic.com and oca.org.
   - Popular modern teaching: I'll look for prosperity or word-of-faith uses of v. 12's "sow… reap" wording and include them only if the allowed sites discuss them.

The finished notes will be in the "v. 1: … (URL)" format you asked for, and I'll leave out anything I can't find.
